verdict.rationale: Firestore docs state that it caches actively used data so apps can write, read, listen to, and query data while the device is offline, and Firebase is positioned to 'store and sync' app data. Together these cover the core offline-write story. A 2016 community complaint about missing offline persistence for JS is dated and platform-specific, so it does not concretely contradict the current Firestore claim. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that queued local writes sync automatically on reconnect, conflict-resolution details, per-platform (web) persistence specifics, independent hands-on corroboration.
